newsitem.title: USA: France must seek employability - finmin.
newsitem.headline: France must seek employability - finmin.

text.p: France must try to reduce its unemployment by making people employable rather than introducing Anglo-Saxon style labour market flexibility, French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Saturday.

"Our problem is not at all about the traditional question of labour market flexibility, as much about the ability of people to find a job," he told reporters after a meeting here of the Group of Seven rich nations.
"What is important is to improve the ability of individuals to become employable," he added.
The aim was to get rid of rigidities in the system -- for example inappropriate studies for young people which failed to train them for the job market.
France's new Socialist-led government would also tackle unemployment by reducing the working week.
"We have no interest in flexibility in the Anglo-Saxon sense of the word," he said.
French politicians from both left and right have traditionally rejected the kind of hire-and-fire labor market policies of the United States.
Strauss-Kahn said the right place for flexibility was in the overall system, "what Marxists would call the superstructure."
